title: Greenland belongs to Denmark. Why?
description:
How did a small country in Europe end up with the biggest island on Earth?
Greenland: Viking farms, a missionary, a treaty after Napoleon lost, and a vote it can still take.
Sources: Wikipedia, Statistics Greenland (Jul 2026).
Maps simplified. Borders as recognised by the country each video is about.
cta: Iceland or the Faroes: which island should we explain next? Comment

lines.text: Greenland sits next to Canada, not Europe, yet it belongs to Denmark. Why?
And it's no small corner: Greenland is the biggest island on Earth. Lay Denmark on top of it, and Denmark covers just one sliver.
Stranger still, most of it isn't green at all: 81% of the island lies under one giant sheet of ice.
So who named it Greenland? Over a thousand years ago, Erik the Red, a Viking sailing from Iceland, picked the name, supposedly to tempt settlers.
His farms died out. So how did Denmark get it? A missionary, Hans Egede, sailed from Denmark-Norway, then one kingdom, and started a colony.
Here's the twist. After backing Napoleon and losing, that kingdom had to hand Norway to Sweden, but the treaty left Greenland, Iceland and the Faroe Islands with Denmark.
Iceland broke away long ago. Greenland stayed, and in 1979 it won home rule, with its own parliament in Nuuk, its capital.
Then in 2009 came self-rule, and with it the right to choose independence by its own vote. So the biggest island on Earth stays with Denmark until its 56,945 people decide otherwise.
Iceland or the Faroes: which island should we explain next? Tell me in the comments. And look again at that map:

fact4 / vote beat ('its 56,831 people'): the figure is out of date. Statistics Greenland gives 56,831 for 1 July 2025 (stat.gl/publ/en/BE/202504, Midyear Population), not 1 Jan 2025 as the fact's as_of says (1 Jan 2025 was 56,542). It has since been superseded by 56,945 on 1 July 2026 (stat.gl/publ/en/BE/202604, 'Record High Mid-Year Population'). Fix: use value 56945, as_of 2026-07-01, source Statistics Greenland, url https://stat.gl/publ/en/BE/202604/contents/Midyear%20Population.htm, and update the description's source line.

Confirmed (no change needed): area 2,166,086 km2, ice sheet 1,755,637 km2 and 81%, home rule 1 May 1979, self-rule 21 June 2009, Erik the Red from Iceland naming it 'supposedly' to attract settlers, Egede's 1721 Dano-Norwegian mission, Norse settlements dying out (all on en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greenland); Treaty of Kiel leaving Greenland, Iceland and the Faroes with Denmark (Britannica, Treaty of Kiel). Denmark (~43,000 km2, about 2% of Greenland) as 'one sliver' is fair. Tone neutral, no side taken on today's politics; the description ends with the channel disclaimer. Style note: 'the right to choose independence by its own vote' is fair (Self-Government Act ch. 8: a referendum in Greenland), but the Act also needs Inatsisartut's and the Danish parliament's consent, so keep it from going any stronger.
